sources.note: Hybrid+EV filter read live: 35 results across 2 pages within 100 mi, price asc. Separately ran the efficient-gas sweep as a make/model-filtered query (Corolla, Civic, Mazda3, Fit, Yaris, Elantra, Accent, Forte, Rio, Soul, Sentra, Versa, Cruze, Sonic, Focus, Mirage) sorted by LOWEST MILEAGE rather than lowest price - the price-asc all-fuel list is nothing but 200k-mile trucks and SUVs. That surfaced genuine low-mileage gas value for the first time. EPA gate applied: Focus SE (28-31), Kia Forte 2016 (30), Accent (30), Sonic (29-30), Soul (28), 2014 Cruze LS 1.8 (26), 2011 Cruze auto (26-28), pre-2014 Corolla (29-30) and 2012 Civic (31) ALL FAIL the 32 mpg floor and were dropped. Passing: 2018 Cruze LS 1.4T (33), 2015 Sentra CVT (32), 2017 Mirage (39), 2016 Mazda3 (33). Screened out: smart ForTwo x2 (two-seater - no back seat for a child), Highlander Hybrid x2 (large SUV), 2011 Camry Hybrid Grand Junction (207 mi - outside radius), 2013 BMW ActiveHybrid 3 (BMW hybrid running costs).

BEST SOURCE THIS RUN. The bare price-asc URL returns 3,502 sponsored trucks/SUVs and is useless, but adding fuelTypes=HYBRID&fuelTypes=ELECTRIC narrows it to 11 in-radius vehicles with deal ratings attached. That surfaced four Nissan Leafs that the Cars.com hybrid list either missed or priced differently - most importantly a 2017 Leaf S at $5,999/63,195 mi only 10 mi away, which is the 2017+ Leaf the criteria specifically prefer. Also found a 2016 Leaf SL (30 kWh) at $7,888 with just 37,994 mi. CarGurus lists the 2018 Leaf SL at $7,882 vs Cars.com's $7,293 - a fee-disclosure difference, not two cars; kept the CarGurus entry since it carries the deal rating. IMV dollar deltas are not exposed on the tiles, only the rating label, so imvDelta is null throughout.

Ran query=prius (258 results) and query=hybrid live. Both are heavily polluted by dealer keyword-spam (Pammi Motors, One Stop, Auto Integrity listing Savanas, Rogues and Land Rovers under hybrid searches), so results were model-filtered. PRICE DROP: the 2015 Chevrolet Volt at One Stop Motors is now $8,999, down $500 from $9,499 on 8/12, and now has a direct posting URL instead of a search link. New but rejected: 2011 Fusion Hybrid at $3,988 (253k mi - too far gone), 2008 Civic Hybrid $2,888 (212k mi + IMA battery risk), 2016 Fusion Energi $6,799 (191k mi). Kept the 2014 Volt at $6,999/151k from Greeley as a cheap PHEV option.

Logged in and fully working. Ran prius, hybrid, nissan leaf, chevy volt, camry hybrid, fusion hybrid, corolla and mazda 3, each scrolled 5-8 times. Marketplace supply is genuinely thin right now, not blocked: 'chevy volt' and 'nissan leaf' return an explicit 'No listings found within 100 miles' page (verified by screenshot, not by an empty selector). Reconfirmed live: 2012 Sonata Hybrid SE $5,500 Denver and 2010 Camry Hybrid LE $5,950 Englewood - and this run captured their REAL item URLs instead of the generic search links used previously, so the tracker can now deep-link them. The 2008 Camry Hybrid $5,999 is still live but was edged out of the top 25. Corolla results were all pre-2014 (29-30 mpg, below the floor) plus a $3,500 '2015 corolla edition s' posted simultaneously in three different cities at the same price - a scam pattern, ignored. FB photo URLs are signed and expire within days, so photo is left null.
2,128 hybrid cars in inventory but the price=0-10000 query param is ignored - the site's own cheapest filter chip is 'Under $20,000 (135)'. No sub-$10k stock, same as prior runs.

Read the Motors Buy-It-Now prius search live (12 listings). All show 'Located in United States' with no real local distance. The only sub-$10k newer car was a 2017 Prius at $9,000 with 235,356 miles - rejected on mileage.

Searched prius live, 13 results with mileage on the tiles. Reconfirmed 2016 Prius c $7,500/100k Aurora. NEW: 2014 Toyota Prius $10,000/112k in Aurora - the newest-generation Prius here with reasonable miles, right at the budget cap. The 2012 Prius v at $8,999/146k is the same car as the Craigslist $8,600 listing and was collapsed; the Craigslist price is lower so neither made the final 25 this run.
hertzcarsales.com returned a bare Tomcat 'HTTP Status 404 - Not Found' page for the Denver price search. Third consecutive run with this failure - the URL layout appears to be permanently gone.

Searched this run as instructed, not skipped. Tried THREE URL layouts live - /used-cars-trucks-suvs/search.html?location=Denver, /list/used-cars/?zip=80015 and /inventory?zip=80015 - all three render Enterprise's own '404 Page Not Found' screen (site chrome loads fine and shows 'Your Dealership: Thornton 80234', so the site is up and it is the search paths that are broken). Their published price tiers still start at 'Under $20k' regardless.

Utah-only inventory, roughly 350+ mi from 80015 and far outside the 100-mi radius. Not stretching the radius this run - the Front Range market produced 25 qualifying cars including two brand-new sub-$8k Leafs.

listings.mpg: 112 MPGe (30 kWh pack, ~107 mi range new)
listings.carSeatNotes: Leaf hatchback has a flat, wide rear bench and tall door openings - one of the easiest cars here for lifting a child into a rear-facing seat, and the hatch takes a stroller plus daycare bags.
listings.nextAction: Dealer - ask for a battery capacity-bar photo or LeafSpy report BEFORE driving out, and confirm it is the 30 kWh 2017 S (some early-build 2017 S cars shipped with the 24 kWh pack).
listings.why: The single best find this run and the exact car the criteria call for: a 2017-or-newer Leaf, only 10 mi away, at $5,999 with 63k miles. The 2017 S uses the 30 kWh pack (~107 mi when new), so even with normal degradation it has a large margin over the ~25 mi daily commute and charges fine on the Level 1 outlet overnight. Cheapest car on this list by a wide margin and the lowest running cost. NHTSA never assigned the 2017 Leaf an overall star rating, so that field is honestly null - offset that by confirming battery health.

listings.carSeatNotes: Modern Prius liftback - roomy rear seat with proper LATCH anchors and top tether; rear-facing fits easily and the big hatch swallows a stroller and daycare bags.
listings.nextAction: Dealer (4301 Morrison Rd) - request the Carfax, confirm it is genuinely the plug-in Prime and not a standard Prius, and check the 62k miles against service records.
listings.why: Still the newest and safest car on the list by four model years. A 2022 plug-in with ~25 mi electric range covers the entire daily commute on the home Level 1 outlet, then returns 54 mpg on gas for trips - no range anxiety at all. 5-star NHTSA and only 1 open recall. Reconfirmed live at $8,950/62k. The only caution is that a 2022 Prime at this price is well under market, so verify the title and history carefully.

listings.mpg: 112 MPGe (30 kWh pack, ~107 mi range new)
listings.carSeatNotes: Same easy flat rear bench as the other Leafs; SL trim adds heated rear seats, which is a real winter perk with a child in the back.
listings.nextAction: Dealer - get the battery capacity bars (12 is full) or a LeafSpy readout before the 36 mi drive to Boulder; at only 38k miles this pack should still be near-healthy.
listings.why: Only 37,994 miles - the lowest-mileage car on the entire list. Critically this is the SL trim, which in 2016 means the 30 kWh battery (~107 mi new), not the weak 24 kWh pack that makes older Leafs a gamble. Very low miles plus the bigger pack means this is the least degraded EV here. 4-star NHTSA. Trade-offs are the 36 mi trip to Boulder and a merely 'Fair Deal' rating - Leaf resale is soft, so there may be room to negotiate.

listings.carSeatNotes: Midsize sedan with a wide rear bench and unobstructed LATCH anchors - a rear-facing seat fits with room to spare behind the front passenger, and the trunk is full-size.
listings.nextAction: Private seller (Elijah on Cars.com) - ask for the VIN and a photo of the title, and confirm hybrid-battery health. No dealer Carfax here, so budget ~$150 for an independent pre-purchase inspection.
listings.why: The best combination of low miles, closeness and price among the conventional hybrids: 89k miles at $7,350, only 6 mi away, 5-star NHTSA and just 2 open recalls. Roomy midsize sedan at 37 mpg - the easiest car here to live with day to day for car-seat duty. Being a private sale it needs more diligence than the dealer cars, which is the only reason it sits behind the two EVs and the Prime.

listings.carSeatNotes: Midsize sedan with a roomy rear bench and easy LATCH access - rear-facing installs comfortably; deep trunk for the stroller.
listings.nextAction: Dealer (Springs Automotive Group) - request the free Carfax and written proof the 9 model-year recall campaigns were performed; confirm hybrid-battery health before making the 55 mi trip.
listings.why: Unchanged at $6,794 with 91,747 miles and still a Cars.com 'Great Deal' - the lowest-mileage Fusion Hybrid available and a genuinely roomy, safe family sedan at 38 mpg. The Fusion Hybrid's nickel-metal-hydride pack has a good long-term reliability record. The catch is the 55 mi drive to Colorado Springs and 9 open recall campaigns to verify; the Lakewood car below is the local alternative at $1,196 more.

listings.carSeatNotes: The Sentra has an unusually large rear seat for a compact - class-leading rear legroom - so a rear-facing seat installs without forcing the front passenger forward. Good pick if the driver is tall.
listings.nextAction: Dealer - request the Carfax and specifically ask about CVT service history; Nissan CVTs of this era are the known weak point, so a transmission fluid record or a test drive watching for shudder matters more than anything else on this car.
listings.why: The best pure-gas car this run and proof the new gas criteria are earning their keep: 70,734 miles at $7,990, a Cars.com 'Great Deal', only 19 mi away, and it clears the fuel-economy floor at exactly 32 mpg combined. No traction battery to worry about and no charging logistics - the simplest, lowest-risk ownership on this whole list, with the roomiest rear seat of any compact here. Ranked behind the hybrids purely because 32 mpg costs meaningfully more per month than a 50 mpg Prius or an EV.

listings.carSeatNotes: Midsize sedan with a wide, flat rear bench and easy LATCH - rear-facing fits comfortably, and the trunk stays full-size despite the battery.
listings.nextAction: Dealer (Mercedes-Benz of Denver) - request the Carfax and confirm hybrid-battery health at 143k miles; with a $501 drop already on the board there is likely more room to negotiate.
listings.why: PRICE DROP: down $501 to $7,098 from $7,599 on 8/12, and Cars.com downgraded its own label from 'Good Deal' to 'Fair Deal' - a car the dealer is actively trying to move, which is negotiating leverage. One of the newest and closest sedans here (2016, 10 mi) with 5-star NHTSA and 37 mpg. The 143k miles is the real trade-off, so the hybrid battery check is not optional.

listings.title: Clean
listings.carSeatNotes: Compact hatchback rear seat - rear-facing fits, but the battery pack raises the cargo floor and eats trunk space, so check clearance behind the front passenger with the seat actually installed.
listings.nextAction: Dealer (Auto Warehouse) - request the free Carfax and confirm realistic winter range before committing to the 71 mi drive to Fort Collins.
listings.why: The only car here with a documented clean title AND 'no accidents reported' AND 5-star NHTSA, at 33,749 miles. ~76 mi of range is ample for a 25 mi round trip on Level 1 charging. Two real drawbacks keep it out of the top five: 71 mi away is the furthest listing on the list, and the Focus Electric's battery has no active thermal management, so Colorado winter range drops harder than the Leaf's.

listings.carSeatNotes: IMPORTANT: the 1st-gen Volt has only TWO rear seats separated by a fixed battery tunnel down the middle. A single rear-facing seat fits fine, but there is no centre position and no room for a second child seat later.
listings.nextAction: Dealer (Frontline) - request the Carfax and the recall receipt, and ask for the battery state-of-health readout. Take the child seat along to the test drive and physically install it before buying.
listings.why: Cheapest way into a plug-in: ~35 mi of electric range covers the whole daily commute on the Level 1 outlet, with a gas engine removing all range anxiety. 5-star NHTSA and only 1 open recall - the cleanest recall record here. Volt battery packs are liquid-cooled and have aged notably better than early Leaf packs. The two-seat rear bench is a genuine long-term limitation worth thinking about if a second child is possible.

listings.carSeatNotes: Compact sedan with a decent rear bench and clearly marked LATCH anchors; rear-facing fits, though a tall driver should check front-seat clearance first.
listings.nextAction: Dealer (Motor Mesh Automotive) - request the Carfax and ask whether the 1.4L turbo's coolant-loss and PCV issues have been addressed; these engines are known for water-pump and valve-cover failures around this mileage.
listings.why: The newest gas car on the list at 2018 with 70,100 miles, 5-star NHTSA, a Cars.com 'Great Deal', and 33 mpg combined from the 1.4L turbo - comfortably clear of the fuel-economy floor. Modern safety kit and no battery to worry about. Held back by the 55 mi drive and by the 1.4T's mediocre reliability record versus a Toyota or the Sentra; the note above is the specific thing to ask about.

listings.carSeatNotes: Golf hatchback with a solid, upright rear bench and wide-opening doors - one of the easier cars here for getting a child in and out, with a usable hatch.
listings.nextAction: Dealer (Victory Motors) - request the Carfax and a battery capacity check. Note Cars.com now rates it 'Good Deal' where it was 'Great Deal' on 8/12, so the pricing edge has narrowed slightly.
listings.why: The most efficient car on the list at 116 MPGe, in the best-built body shell of any EV here - the e-Golf drives like a normal Golf rather than an economy car. ~83 mi of rated range is plenty for the short commute on Level 1. Downgraded from 'Great Deal' this run. NHTSA never issued an overall rating for the e-Golf, hence the null, and VW's EV service network in Colorado is thinner than Nissan's.

listings.carSeatNotes: Full midsize Camry rear bench - the most generous rear-facing clearance of any car on this list, plus a big trunk for daycare bags and a stroller.
listings.nextAction: Private seller - the listing still does not state mileage, so ask for the odometer reading, the VIN and a photo of the title before anything else; then confirm traction-battery health on a 16-year-old hybrid.
listings.why: Now deep-linked to its real Marketplace posting rather than a search URL. The Camry Hybrid drivetrain is among the most durable ever built and this is a lot of safe, roomy family car for $5,950 only 12 mi away. Two honest caveats keep it mid-pack: the seller still has not published the mileage, and 9 open recall campaigns for this model year need checking.

listings.carSeatNotes: Midsize sedan with a wide rear bench and easy LATCH - rear-facing seat fits comfortably; large trunk.
listings.nextAction: Private seller - ask for the VIN, the mileage and a title photo, then check the VIN against Hyundai's engine recall campaigns. This generation had a widely reported Theta II engine failure issue, so a documented engine replacement or the recall inspection receipt is the single most important thing to see.
listings.why: The cheapest midsize hybrid on the list at $5,500, 12 mi away, 5-star NHTSA and 36 mpg. Reconfirmed live on Facebook and now deep-linked to the actual posting. Ranked here rather than higher specifically because of the Theta II engine history on 2011-2014 Sonatas plus 6 open recalls and undisclosed mileage - great value if it checks out, expensive if it does not.

listings.carSeatNotes: Midsize sedan with a roomy rear bench and easy LATCH access - rear-facing seat fits comfortably.
listings.nextAction: Dealer (Urban Motors Red) - request the free Carfax and proof the 9 model-year recalls were performed.
listings.why: The local alternative to the Colorado Springs Fusion Hybrid: same car and same 'Great Deal' rating, 18 mi away instead of 55, for $1,196 more and 9,590 more miles. If a Saturday round trip to Colorado Springs is unappealing, this is the one to look at. VIN confirmed and carried forward unchanged.

listings.mpg: 114 MPGe (24 kWh pack, ~84 mi range new)
listings.carSeatNotes: Flat, roomy rear bench and wide door opening make the rear-facing install easy; usable hatch for daycare gear.
listings.nextAction: Dealer (Alimari Auto Sales) - insist on a battery capacity-bar count before making the 54 mi drive; on a 24 kWh car anything below 10 bars makes winter range marginal.
listings.why: Cheap at $6,495 with reasonable 72,846 miles, but note carefully that this is the S trim, which in 2016 means the smaller 24 kWh pack (~84 mi new) rather than the 30 kWh pack in the SL at rank 3. After a decade of degradation, real winter range could be near 50 mi - still fine for a 25 mi round trip, but with far less margin than the 2017 or the SL. Ranked below both for that reason, plus the 54 mi trip.

listings.carSeatNotes: Roomy midsize sedan - wide rear doors and easy LATCH make a rear-facing install comfortable, and the trunk stays usable despite the plug-in battery.
listings.nextAction: Dealer (Car Depot) - request the Carfax, confirm the ~29 mi EV range still holds, and check hybrid-battery health at 127k miles.
listings.why: The newest plug-in besides the Prime and the roomiest: ~29 mi of electric range covers the full daily commute on the Level 1 outlet, then 40 mpg on gas. 5-star NHTSA with only 2 open recalls and it is close by at 15 mi. The 127k miles on a complex plug-in drivetrain is what keeps it out of the top ten - the battery health check matters more here than on any other car in the top half.

listings.carSeatNotes: CAUTION: the Prius c is a subcompact on the Yaris platform, noticeably smaller than a regular Prius. A rear-facing seat fits but usually forces the front passenger seat well forward - install the actual seat before buying if the front passenger is tall.
listings.nextAction: Private seller in Aurora - ask for the VIN and a title photo, confirm the ~100k mileage, and take the child seat to the test drive. Easiest local viewing of anything on this list.
listings.why: The closest car on the list at 5 mi and the cheapest 50 mpg option, with Toyota hybrid reliability and 100k miles. Perfect on paper for a short commute. The one real reservation is size - it is the smallest car here by interior volume, which matters for daily rear-facing car-seat duty, so it is ranked on merit rather than on its excellent running costs alone.

listings.carSeatNotes: Same two-seat rear bench limitation as the 2011 Volt - a fixed battery tunnel runs down the middle, so one rear-facing seat fits but there is no third position.
listings.nextAction: Dealer (One Stop Motors) - request the Carfax and battery state of health. The price has now moved twice, so open with an offer meaningfully below $8,999.
listings.why: PRICE DROP: now $8,999, down $500 from $9,499 on 8/12, and it finally has a direct posting URL instead of a search link. The newest Volt here with ~38 mi of electric range, 5-star NHTSA and just 1 open recall. Same two-rear-seat caveat as the 2011 car, and at $8,999 with 107k miles it is expensive next to the $5,995 2011 Volt - the extra money buys four model years and slightly more range.

listings.mpg: 112 MPGe (40 kWh pack, ~151 mi range new)
listings.carSeatNotes: Second-generation Leaf - larger and better finished inside than the 2011-2017 cars, with a wide flat rear bench and excellent door openings for loading a child.
listings.nextAction: Dealer (South Colorado Motors) - get a LeafSpy or capacity-bar reading; 124k miles on an air-cooled 40 kWh pack is exactly the situation where degradation shows, so this number decides whether the car is worth the trip. Cars.com lists the same car at $7,293 before fees - use that as a negotiating anchor.
listings.why: The newest EV on the list and the only 40 kWh Leaf (~151 mi when new), so even substantially degraded it has real range margin. 'Good Deal' on CarGurus. Two things hold it back: 124,667 miles is by far the highest of any EV here, and the 2018 Leaf's passively cooled pack degrades faster with high mileage. Note the price discrepancy - CarGurus shows $7,882 including fees, Cars.com $7,293 without.

listings.carSeatNotes: Full-size Prius liftback - roomy rear seat, easy rear-facing fit and a large hatch that takes a stroller plus daycare bags without folding seats.
listings.nextAction: Dealer (Car Corner) - request the Carfax and confirm the 3 recall campaigns were completed; at 178k ask specifically about the inverter water pump and any hybrid warning lights.
listings.why: Bulletproof third-generation Prius, 5-star NHTSA, only 12 mi away and a Cars.com 'Great Deal' at $7,999. Note the EPA combined figure is 48 mpg, not the 50 often quoted - that is the revised official rating. The 178,177 miles is high, but this generation routinely runs past 250k and running costs are among the lowest here.

listings.carSeatNotes: CAUTION: this is the smallest and lightest car on the list. A rear-facing seat physically fits, but rear space is tight and the Mirage's low curb weight is a real disadvantage in a collision with a larger vehicle - worth weighing carefully for a car whose main job is carrying a young child.
listings.nextAction: Dealer (Mike Shaw) - request the Carfax; also test drive it on I-25 or E-470 specifically, because the 78 hp 3-cylinder struggles to merge at altitude with passengers aboard.
listings.why: Highest gas fuel economy available at 39 mpg combined, low miles at 68,597, a 'Good Deal' rating and Mitsubishi's long powertrain warranty history. It qualifies on the stated criteria and is cheap to run. It is ranked low deliberately: it is the least safe-feeling and slowest option here, and the safety of a very light subcompact is a legitimate consideration given the buyer's priority of a safe car for a young child. Included for completeness rather than recommended.

listings.carSeatNotes: Best body shape on the list for daily child duty - a tall hybrid hatchback with an upright rear seat and wide doors, so you lift the child in rather than bending down, and the hatch takes a stroller easily.
listings.nextAction: Dealer (Mike Shaw Subaru) - request the Carfax and confirm the door-latch and shifter-bushing recall campaigns were performed.
listings.why: The most practical body style here for a parent: tall, upright, easy loading, big hatch, and 40 mpg. Price is holding at $7,258 after ticking up on 8/12. Ranked in the twenties because of 137k miles, no NHTSA overall rating on record, and the C-Max's below-average reliability scores relative to a Prius - but if daily practicality outweighs long-term reliability, move it up.

listings.carSeatNotes: Roomy Prius liftback rear seat; easy rear-facing fit and a big hatch for stroller plus daycare bags.
listings.nextAction: Private party - verify clean title, get the maintenance records, and ask to see the recent-inspection paperwork the ad claims.
listings.why: The same red 2014 Prius Two, still listed at $7,550 with 145k miles and a claimed recent inspection. Newer generation than the 2013 above and $449 cheaper with 33k fewer miles, but it is a private sale with no dealer history, which is why it sits lower. 14 mi away and reconfirmed live this run.

listings.carSeatNotes: Compact sedan with a firm, well-shaped rear bench and good LATCH access; rear-facing fits, but rear legroom is tighter than the Sentra so check front-seat clearance.
listings.nextAction: Dealer - request the Carfax and check the 6 open recall campaigns for this model year, several of which relate to the Takata airbag inflators.
listings.why: Clears the fuel-economy floor at 33 mpg combined with 5-star NHTSA and Mazda's strong reliability record - by reputation the best-built gas car on this list and much better to drive than the Cruze or Mirage. Held back by price: $8,999 for 91,216 miles is the weakest price-per-mile of the three qualifying gas cars, and it carries 6 open recalls to verify.

listings.carSeatNotes: Full-size Prius liftback - roomy rear seat, easy rear-facing install, and the largest cargo hatch of any Prius generation short of the v wagon.
listings.nextAction: Private seller in Aurora - ask for the VIN and title photo and confirm the 112k mileage. Right at the budget cap, so negotiate: offer around $9,000 given it is a private sale with no history report.
listings.why: The lowest-mileage third-generation Prius found this run (112k) and it is 5 mi away in Aurora. Excellent car underneath - 48 mpg, Toyota reliability, roomy hatch. Ranked last purely on price: at exactly $10,000 it hits the budget ceiling and costs $2,450 more than the 2014 Prius Two at rank 23 for 33k fewer miles. Worth pursuing only if the seller will move on price.
